items.text: – Viiiiish, Baba, Baba, clòmpami custa pupixedda manna manna?
items.q: On the street, a stranger's little girl asks her dad for a big doll. Does it sound like baby talk?
before: – Amir, Amir-jan, fizu meu. Isveglia·ti. Isveglia·ti pro sa Maman. Totu fiat unu sonnu. Non tènnere timoria, seo inoghe.

…pro mi guidare. Una lugore chi lampizat in sa manu de una fizeddu de qui no apo mai ischidu in cale colore de sa boèsta de lapis de colores s'ajustaiat sa janna de domo sua. Benit currende una pitzinna faghende su sonu de su giogatolu sou e s'arrestat acanta mia. Càstiat is giogatolos. Narat:

items.text: – Càstia comente si la coghet, ti cagas su tzérebru.
items.q: Someone scolds a friend: look what a mess you made. Is that clear?
before: – E tue puru ses unu Rashid.
S'Eskandar si furriat cara a mie e avantzat sa conca e su pettus cara a mie. Teniat is ogros meda abertos, e cun unu tonu rude, sena perdere pro custu s'aria sua a s'Alain Delon, at naradu:

items.text: E tue, cun cussu modu tuo de fueddare de cazu, su nùmene tuo diat dèpere èssere Alain Cazon.
items.q: 'Alain Cazon' is meant as a rude pun on the actor Alain Delon. Would Sardinian readers get it? If not, what word could carry it?
before: – Eja, Hamoun est unu bonu nùmene pro tie. Comente su Hamoun de sa peliculedda, tue puru ses prenu de preguntas. Ses prenu de angustia e ses fonte de disassossegu, no pro tie, ma pro mie.

items.text: Sa proida non falat dae terra a chelu.
items.q: Her son says he would die for her; Maman objects. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Sa manu mia est curtza e s'unione tua est attesu.
items.q: Amir tells the girl he loves why he holds back. A Persian expression kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Su chi naro est chi, si restas inoghe sètzidu leghende poesia, no ti si at a callentare su pane.
items.q: A friend criticises Amir for reading poetry all day. A Persian expression kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Bibi, chi Deus dda tèngiat in gròria, naraiat in custos momentos: si ddu naro, sa limba mia s'abbrusat; si no ddu naro, sa medudda de is ossos mios s'abbrusat.
items.q: Maman hesitates before criticising her husband. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: – Ghassem torra a fàghere is fainas suas, narat «un'annu bonu si connoschet dae su beranu suo».
items.q: The family's New Year visits were cancelled; a brother jokes about it. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Immoi deo isolvo su filu de is fueddos e tue leadilu, giughe·lu in su mundu tuo, po chi no si ammuntonent inoghe, in su mundu meu.
items.q: You take the words with you. Does this sentence read naturally?
before: …betzos, e nois pigaìamus su filu e giraìamus intro de sa domo po chi su filu de lana non s'ammuntonesset. Forsis sa generatzione tua est arribada unos cantos annos troppu tardu pro connòschere custu mundu de filos, ma imàgina: unu die, in un'incàntu de su mundu, is pipios si trastulaiant gasi.
